title: Two Sum
prompt: Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices `[i, j]` (i < j) of the two numbers that add up to target. Exactly one solution exists. Aim for O(n).

title: Valid Parentheses
prompt: Return True if the string `s` containing only ()[]{} is balanced (every opener closed in the right order), else False.

title: Group Anagrams
prompt: Group words that are anagrams of each other. Return a list of groups; sort the words inside each group and sort the groups (so the output is deterministic).

title: Merge Intervals
prompt: Given a list of `[start, end]` intervals, merge all overlapping ones and return them sorted by start.

title: Top K Frequent Words
prompt: Return the `k` most frequent words. Ties are broken alphabetically.
solution:
from collections import Counter
def top_k(words, k):
    c = Counter(words)
    return sorted(c, key=lambda w: (-c[w], w))[:k]

title: LRU Cache
prompt: Implement class `LRUCache(capacity)` with `get(key)` (return value or -1) and `put(key, value)`. When full, evict the least recently used key. Both O(1). The tests call a helper `run_ops(ops)` you don't need to write.

title: Chunk Text with Overlap (RAG)
prompt: RAG ingestion: split `text` into chunks of at most `size` words, where consecutive chunks share `overlap` words. Return a list of strings (words joined by single spaces). Stop once the last word is included. Assume 0 <= overlap < size.

tests.expr: chunk_words('a b c d e f g', 3, 1)
chunk_words('a b c d e f', 4, 2)

title: Top-K Cosine Similarity (vector search)
prompt: Implement semantic search without libraries: given a `query` vector and a dict `docs` {id: vector}, return the ids of the `k` most similar docs by cosine similarity, highest first (ties: alphabetical id). Skip zero vectors.

title: Token Bucket Rate Limiter
prompt: LLM APIs rate-limit you. Implement `TokenBucket(capacity, refill_per_sec)` with `allow(now)` that returns True if a request at time `now` (seconds, float) may proceed (consuming 1 token), else False. The bucket starts full; tokens refill continuously, capped at capacity.

title: Parse an LLM Tool Call
prompt: LLMs often wrap JSON in prose or ```json fences. Write `parse_tool_call(text)` that extracts the first JSON object in `text` and returns `(name, args)` from keys `name` and `arguments`. If `arguments` is a JSON string, decode it too. Return `None` if no valid object with a `name` key is found.

title: Remove Duplicates, Keep Order
prompt: Return the list with duplicates removed, keeping the first occurrence order. O(n).

title: Longest Substring Without Repeats
prompt: Return the length of the longest substring of `s` without repeating characters.

title: Flatten a Nested List
prompt: Flatten an arbitrarily nested list of integers into a single list.

title: Retry Decorator with Backoff
prompt: Write a decorator factory `retry(times)` so that a decorated function is called up to `times` attempts; if every attempt raises, re-raise the last exception. Return the first successful result. (No real sleeping needed.) The tests use a helper `flaky(n)` you don't need to write - it fails n times, then returns 'ok'.

title: SQL: Departments Above Average
prompt: Table `employees(id, name, dept, salary)`. Return `dept` and average salary `avg_salary` for departments whose average salary is greater than 100, ordered by avg_salary descending. Write only the SELECT query.

tests.name: sample data
tests.setup:
CREATE TABLE employees(id INT, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INT);
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Asha','AI',150),(2,'Ravi','AI',120),(3,'Meera','AI',150),(4,'John','Data',100),(5,'Zoya','Data',130),(6,'Kabir','Ops',90);

solution: SELECT dept, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY dept HAVING AVG(salary) > 100 ORDER BY avg_salary DESC

title: SQL: Top Earner per Department
prompt: Table `employees(id, name, dept, salary)`. Return `dept, name, salary` of the highest-paid employee(s) in each department (include ties), ordered by dept then name. Use a window function.

tests.name: sample data
tests.setup:
CREATE TABLE employees(id INT, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INT);
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Asha','AI',150),(2,'Ravi','AI',120),(3,'Meera','AI',150),(4,'John','Data',100),(5,'Zoya','Data',130),(6,'Kabir','Ops',90);

solution: SELECT dept, name, salary FROM (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) r FROM employees) WHERE r = 1 ORDER BY dept, name

title: SQL: Running Total per User
prompt: Table `orders(id, user_id, day, amount)`. Return `user_id, day, running_total` where running_total is the cumulative sum of amount per user ordered by day. Order the result by user_id, day.
solution: SELECT user_id, day, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY day) AS running_total FROM orders ORDER BY user_id, day
